# Psalm 81 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** To-the-choirmaster. On the-Gittith. Of-Asaph. Sing-aloud to-God our-strength; shout-for-joy to-God-of Jacob.

**2** Raise a-song and-sound the-tambourine, the-lyre pleasant with the-harp.

**3** Blow at-the-new-moon the-trumpet, at-the-full-moon for-day-of our-feast.

**4** For a-statute for-Israel it-is, a-judgment for-God-of Jacob.

**5** A-testimony in-Joseph he-set-it, when-he-went-out over the-land-of Egypt; a-language not I-knew I-heard.

**6** 'I-removed from-the-burden his-shoulder; his-hands from-the-basket were-freed.

**7** In-distress you-called and-I-rescued-you; I-answered-you in-hiding-place-of thunder; I-tested-you at waters-of Meribah. Selah.

**8** Hear O-my-people and-I-will-admonish you; O-Israel if you-will-listen to-me!

**9** Not shall-be among-you a-god foreign, and-not shall-you-bow-down to-a-god alien.

**10** I am-YHWH your-God, the-one-bringing-you-up from-land-of Egypt; open-wide your-mouth and-I-will-fill-it.

**11** But-not listened my-people to-my-voice, and-Israel not was-willing for-me.

**12** And-I-let-them-go in-stubbornness-of their-heart; they-walked in-their-own-counsels.

**13** O-that my-people were-listening to-me, Israel in-my-ways would-walk!

**14** In-a-little their-enemies I-would-subdue, and-against their-adversaries I-would-turn my-hand.

**15** Haters-of YHWH would-cringe before-him, and-their-time would-be to-forever.

**16** And-he-would-feed-him from-finest-of wheat, and-from-the-rock with-honey I-would-satisfy-you.'

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **81:3**: Trumpet (shofar) at the new moon and full moon — likely refers to the Feast of Tabernacles (Sukkot), which begins at the full moon of Tishri.

- **81:10**: 'Open-wide your-mouth and-I-will-fill-it' — stunning image of God's generosity; Israel need only receive.

— EMET
